name: Bamboo Shoot Fry
ingredients: 250g fermented bamboo shoots (tuai), rinsed and drained
1 cup fresh bamboo shoot strips (optional, for texture)
1/2 tsp baking soda (to reduce bitterness, optional)
instructions: 1. If using fresh bamboo shoots, boil them in water with a pinch of baking soda for 10 minutes, then drain and rinse. If using only fermented shoots, skip to step 2.
2. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan until it smokes slightly. Add dried red chilies and fry for 30 seconds until they darken.
3. Add sliced onion and sauté until translucent, about 3-4 minutes. Add garlic and ginger, cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
4. Add turmeric powder, stir well, then add the fermented bamboo shoots (and fresh shoots if using). Cook on high heat for 2 minutes, stirring frequently.
5. Add green chilies and salt. Reduce heat to medium and cook for another 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the shoots are tender and slightly caramelized.
6. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with steamed rice.
description: A smoky, heart-warming embrace of fermented bamboo and mountain herbs.
